2022_250_june_22_accountability_plan_boe.paragraph: A 37-slide staff presentation to the Troy School District Board of Education, dated to the June 14, 2022 meeting, reporting mid-year progress on the Project 2026 Blueprint accountability plan and its four World Class for All pillars: Early Childhood to Career (Green), Equity and Well-Being (Red), Deep Learning (Blue), and Building Capacity (Gold). Each pillar is presented with objectives, key results, January-June 2022 celebrations, challenges, and recommendations. Among the reported results, Career and Technical Education program growth provided almost triple the funding from year 20/21 to 21/22, and a 1.0 social worker was placed at every elementary school.
2022_250_june_22_accountability_plan_boe.page:
## Overview
Project 2026 Blueprint, District / School / Troy - a Troy School District Board of Education presentation of the accountability plan tied to the 2026 Troy School District Blueprint. The deck moves through an Introduction, Key Themes and Next Steps, the four pillars, and a Summary across 37 slides (slides 23-30 and 37 carry no extracted text).

## Framework
Mission and Vision (Re) Fresh restates the Troy School District mission as Ensuring learning for all, centering the ONETROY community, with four pillars: Early Childhood to Career (expands on research with access through career); Equity and Well-Being (ensures safety, belonging, and connection); Deep Learning (ensures learning for all throughout the system); Building Capacity (expands to include students, staff, and community as learners). Core values named are Collaboration, Deep Learning and Focus. The Accountability Plan holds the team accountable to Objectives and Key Results.

## Green Pillar - Early Childhood to Career
Objectives: continue investing in high-quality early childhood education, including advocating for access to universal preschool for all three and four-year-olds; expand college and career pathways for middle and high school students through high-quality career and technical education, expanded computer science access, connections for underrepresented students to in-demand careers, and partnerships with higher education and employers for work-based learning, credentials and college credit.

| Key result | Target |
|---|---|
| Additional GSRP slots requested from the state of Michigan in 2021-22 | 16-32 |
| Additional PreK classrooms opened in 2021-22 | 2-3 (40-60 students) |
| Meetings/site visits with local legislators on free preschool for all | 2 during 2021-22 |
| Building leader reports back from Career Readiness meetings | 2 times during 2021-22 |
| Career Readiness meetings devoted to Portrait of a Graduate research | 2 |

Celebrations (January-June 2022): record-high early childhood enrollment with waitlists for PreK, GSRP, tuition and before/after school programs; CTE growth providing almost triple the funding from year 20/21 to 21/22; k-5 Career Readiness engagement partnered with Media Specialists and Maker Space growth. Challenges: capacity limits; grantee Oakland Schools has not offered access for additional GSRP slots; stigma around Career Readiness.

## Red Pillar - Equity and Well-Being
Objectives: safely reopen schools and support students disproportionately impacted by the pandemic; fund whole-child investments including community schools with wraparound services and more counselors, social workers and school psychologists; assess and act on facility upgrades. Results reported: 1.0 SW at every elementary, increased psychologist support and counseling at secondary; data reviews with interventions in progress; monthly staff topics; a District Level Team established; a 2nd annual equity and inclusion stakeholder survey. Recommendations include SEL pilots for 2022-23.

## Blue Pillar - Deep Learning
MTSS build-out in mathematics: elementary Tier 1 early adopters (70+ teachers) and Tier 2/3 Math Recovery training for 9 teachers; secondary Tier 1 teacher pilot team and Tier 2/3 Math Recovery training for 6 teachers; Math Specialists coaching PD; a Troy High visit to Troy Athens for job-embedded learning. Broader objectives cover technology access, NPDL and The 6 C's, and facilities.

## Gold Pillar - Building Capacity
Educator preparation, pipelines for underrepresented educators, and job-embedded learning. Reported partnerships include MSU Create for Stem, Teachers College, National Equity Project, and Oakland University as exclusive Elementary COE partner. Challenges include teacher coverage, calendar time for collaboration, and teacher shortage particularly in special education.
2022_250_june_22_accountability_plan_boe.verbose:
Project 2026 Blueprint is a 37-slide Troy School District staff presentation to the Board of Education carried on the June 14, 2022 agenda under the title June 22 Accountability Plan BOE Presentation. Its title slide reads Project 2026 Blueprint / District / School / Troy. The deck is organized as an Introduction (2026 Troy School District Blueprint), Key Themes and Next Steps, four pillar sections, and a Summary. Slides 23 through 30 and slide 37 contain no extracted text.

Mission and Vision (Re) Fresh. The framing slide places the Troy School District mission at the center - Mission: Ensuring learning for all. Centers ONETROY community - surrounded by four pillars, each with a one-line refresh: EARLY CHILDHOOD TO CAREER expands on research with access through career; EQUITY AND WELL-BEING ensures safety, belonging, and connection; DEEP LEARNING ensures learning for all throughout the system; BUILDING CAPACITY expands to include students, staff, and community as learners.

Core Values and Accountability Plan. The World Class for All Pillars are described as carefully aligned to the district core values of Collaboration, Deep Learning and Focus. The Accountability Plan slide states that the World Class for All Pillars hold the team accountable to Objectives and Key Results.

Green Pillar - Early Childhood to Career. The section covers Overview, Objectives and Key Results. Objectives are to continue to invest in high-quality early childhood education, including advocating for access to universal preschool for all three and four-year-olds; and to expand college and career pathways for middle and high school students, with a plan aimed at providing more students access to high-quality career and technical education programs that expand access to computer science, connect underrepresented students to careers in demand in high-growth industry sectors, and include partnerships with institutions of higher education, employers and other stakeholders allowing students to engage in quality work-based learning opportunities, earn a credential, and/or earn college credit.

Green Pillar Key Results: apply for 16-32 additional GSRP slots from the state of Michigan in the 2021-22 school year; open an additional 2-3 PreK classrooms (40-60 students) in the 2021-22 school year; schedule two meetings and/or site visits with local legislators regarding free preschool for all during the 2021-22 school year; building leaders will participate in Career Readiness meetings led by district CR team leaders and report back to their respective building teams two times during the 2021-22 school year; the Green Pillar Team will research the Portrait of a Graduate framework to implement the process in TSD during two Career Readiness meetings; and the Green Pillar Team will develop a Portrait of a Graduate survey by the close of the 2021-22 school year.

Green Pillar January-June 2022 Celebrations: current Early Childhood enrollment at a record high, with waitlists for PreK, GSRP, tuition and before and after school programs; Portrait of a Graduate work investigating other districts, with the team having met and created a timeline for the process and for engaging all stakeholders; CTE program growth that has provided almost triple the funding from year 20/21 to 21/22 for program improvements, creating new learning opportunities for students; Career Readiness engagement opportunities in k-5 partnered with Media Specialists and Maker Space growth; and continued prioritization of post-secondary learning partnerships in various ways throughout k-12.

Green Pillar January 2022 Challenges: the current capacity limit for early childhood programs; grantee Oakland Schools has not offered access for additional GSRP slots; alignment of Media/Maker with Career Readiness in terms of time and consistency; the need to mindshift the stigma of CR to help prioritize relevance to learning in classrooms; and balancing Portrait of a Graduate work with current top priorities.

Green Pillar January 2022 Recommendations: early and frequent Early Childhood recruitment for 2022-23; align PreK enrollment with Kindergarten enrollment; continued advocacy for universal funding; prioritize messaging Career Readiness as a tool for students aligned with academic planning and college readiness with administrators, teachers and counselors; and Portrait of a Graduate work through ILT team partnerships.

Red Pillar - Equity and Well-Being. Objectives: safely reopen schools and support students, particularly those disproportionately impacted by the pandemic; fund additional investments to support the needs of the whole child, including community schools that provide wraparound services like afterschool programs and hiring more counselors, social workers and school psychologists; and assess the need and take action for upgraded facilities to meet the demands of a world class learning environment in all school communities.

Red Pillar Key Results: increase Social Work and Counseling support in all buildings; review and monitor student data; emphasis on adult learning in the areas of well-being and equity; create common understanding of a system of support at all levels; and development of a district level Equity Leader network. The January-June 2022 status slide reports 1.0 SW at every elementary with increased psychologist support and counseling at secondary; data reviews conducted with interventions in progress; monthly staff topics; and a District Level Team established. A second January-June 2022 slide adds a presentation to the board on Social Work, Counseling and Psychologist support; continued reviews and exploration of additional intervention options; conducting a 2nd annual equity and inclusion stakeholder survey; monthly staff topics plus district-wide learning on Equity; and a District Level Team that will create systems to support well being.

Red Pillar Recommendations: continue Social Work, Psychologist and Counseling support in all buildings; resource implementation for support tied to student data review; monthly staff topics, district-wide learning on Equity, and evaluation of progress and future goals through equity data analysis; SEL pilots for 2022-23; and development of the district level Equity Leader network.

Blue Pillar - Deep Learning. Objectives: create and sustain systems of support at all levels that deepen learning and empower student voice (MTSS), with access to deep learning described as imperative for all children; improve technology access for students and families while providing quality training to leverage technology to deepen learning; continue to pursue the global best practices of all content areas (NPDL, The 6 C's, Learning partnerships); and assess the need and take action for upgraded facilities.

Blue Pillar Key Results center on mathematics MTSS. For Elementary Math MTSS: Tier 1 Early Adopters (70+ teachers); Tier 2/3 Math Recovery Training for 9 teachers; a Board visit to observe; and principal learning. For Secondary Math MTSS: a Tier 1 teacher pilot team with early research classrooms; Tier 2/3 Math Recovery Training for 6 teachers; and principal learning. Also listed are Math Specialists Coaching PD, a visit to elementary to observe coaching, a Troy High visit to Troy Athens for job-embedded learning, and middle school math specialists planning colleague observations.

Blue Pillar Recommendations: formalize review of data at the building level for both elementary and secondary; next level training in Math Recovery for elementary and middle school math specialists; continue course offerings for elementary and special-education teachers; support the early adopter team with job-embedded learning; support the middle school pilot team with job-embedded learning; and have Math Specialists expand classroom coaching.

Gold Pillar - Building Capacity of Students, Staff, and Families. Objectives: improving educator preparation, strengthening pipelines for underrepresented educators, and supporting current educators; continuing to provide job-embedded professional learning experiences for all staff; and providing professional learning opportunities for staff, community and students with the goal of co-designing impactful experiences to better the OneTroy community.

Gold Pillar Key Results and January-June 2022 Celebrations: all elementary staff had two job-embedded learning experiences utilizing technology to enhance teaching and learning; Elementary Math Specialists trained in MSRP1, the Math Recovery Intensive Intervention Course; Middle and High School Math Specialists trained in AVMR, the Fractions Math Recovery Course; high school chemistry job-embedded learning with the MSU Create for Stem Partnership; a PreK-12 Coaching Institute with Teachers College including classroom visits at Larson and Troy High; buildings partnered with the National Equity Project to conduct student leadership and student voice sessions; Board of Education learning at Costello; an Equity Parent Advisory Committee; and an Oakland University partnership with the Elementary COE as exclusive partner.

Gold Pillar Challenges: teacher coverage for job-embedded learning; the need for time built into the calendar for teacher collaboration; parent education around changes in teaching and learning in the Troy School District; finding candidates with diverse backgrounds who want to apply or relocate for positions in the area; and teacher shortage, particularly in special education.

Gold Pillar Recommendations: host meetings that do not occur in classrooms after or before school at the curriculum rate; host a parent learning series around deep learning and changes to education; extend the conversation with Oakland University into secondary, in particular AP and science candidates; establish a partnership with Eastern Michigan's Special Education COE; join the PTO Advisory Board for more in-depth learning around mathematics; and work as a teaching and learning team to create a workplan based on the biggest priorities, named as Secondary Technology Support, Math Early Adopter Team, and Elementary Social Studies. The deck closes with a Summary slide for the 2026 Troy School District Blueprint.

2022_251_l_4029.page:
## Document type
Michigan Department of Treasury Form 614 (Rev. 02-22), designated L-4029, titled 2022 Tax Rate Request / MILLAGE REQUEST REPORT TO COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS. Routing is printed at the top: ORIGINAL TO County Clerk(s) and the Michigan Department of Treasury; COPY TO Equalization Department(s); COPY TO each township or city clerk. The form must be completed and submitted on or before September 30, 2022. It is issued under authority of MCL Sections 211.24e, 211.34 and 211.34d; filing is mandatory and a penalty applies, with the penalty for non-filing provided under MCL Sec 211.119.

## Header fields
County(ies) where the local government unit levies taxes; 2022 Taxable Value of ALL Properties in the Unit as of 5-23-2022; Local Government Unit Requesting Millage Levy; and, for LOCAL school districts, the 2022 Taxable Value excluding Principal Residence, Qualified Agricultural, Qualified Forest, Industrial Personal and Commercial Personal Properties. In this copy all header fields are blank.

## Column structure
| Col | Heading |
|---|---|
| 1 | Source |
| 2 | Purpose of Millage |
| 3 | Date of Election |
| 4 | Original Millage Authorized by Election, Charter, etc. |
| 5 | 2021 Millage Rate Permanently Reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee |
| 6 | 2022 Current Year Headlee Millage Reduction Fraction |
| 7 | 2022 Millage Rate Permanently Reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee |
| 8 | Sec. 211.34 Truth in Assessing or Equalization Millage Rollback Fraction |
| 9 | Maximum Allowable Millage Levy |
| 10 | Millage Requested to be Levied July 1 |
| 11 | Millage Requested to be Levied Dec. 1 |
| 12 | Expiration Date of Millage Authorized |

## Certification
Signature blocks are provided for Prepared by, Telephone Number, Title of Preparer and Date; for the Clerk or Secretary; and for the Chairperson or President. The certification states that representatives of the local government unit certify the requested tax levy rates have been reduced if necessary to comply with the state constitution (Article 9, Section 31) and with MCL Sections 211.24e and 211.34, and, for LOCAL school districts levying a Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millage, MCL 380.1211(3). A footnote adds that under Truth in Taxation, MCL Section 211.24e, the governing body may levy a rate not exceeding the maximum authorized rate in column 9.

## Local school district section
A Local School District Use Only block, to be completed if requesting millage to be levied per STC Bulletin 2 of 2022, captures Total School District Operating Rates to be Levied (HH/Supp and NH Oper ONLY) broken out for Principal Residence, Qualified Ag., Qualified Forest and Industrial Personal; for Commercial Personal; and for all Other.

## Instructions
Page 2 provides column-by-column instructions issued under MCL Sections 211.24e (truth in taxation), 211.34 (truth in county equalization and truth in assessing), 211.34d (Headlee), and 211.36 and 211.37 (apportionment), including references to Form 2166 (L-4034) millage reduction fraction calculations, STC Bulletin No. 11 of 1999 as supplemented by letter of 6/7/2000, and a memo to assessors dated October 26, 2004 regarding the change in the collection date of certain county taxes.
2022_251_l_4029.verbose:
Form 614 (Rev. 02-22), the L-4029, is the Michigan Department of Treasury 2022 Tax Rate Request, formally the MILLAGE REQUEST REPORT TO COUNTY BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS, included in the Troy School District Board of Education materials for the June 14, 2022 meeting. The distribution instruction printed at the top directs the ORIGINAL TO County Clerk(s) and the Michigan Department of Treasury, a COPY TO Equalization Department(s), and a COPY TO each township or city clerk. The form must be completed and submitted on or before September 30, 2022, and the filer is directed to carefully read the instructions on page 2. The form is issued under the authority of MCL Sections 211.24e, 211.34 and 211.34d; filing is mandatory and a penalty applies. The form must be completed for each unit of government for which a property tax is levied, and the penalty for non-filing is provided under MCL Sec 211.119. The form states that the tax rates listed have been authorized for levy on the 2022 tax roll. In this copy the data fields are blank; the extracted text consists of the printed headings, certification language and instructions.

Header data fields. The form asks for the county or counties where the local government unit levies taxes; the 2022 Taxable Value of ALL Properties in the Unit as of 5-23-2022; the Local Government Unit Requesting Millage Levy; and, for LOCAL school districts, the 2022 Taxable Value excluding Principal Residence, Qualified Agricultural, Qualified Forest, Industrial Personal and Commercial Personal Properties.

The twelve reporting columns are: (1) Source; (2) Purpose of Millage; (3) Date of Election; (4) Original Millage Authorized by Election, Charter, etc.; (5) 2021 Millage Rate Permanently Reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee; (6) 2022 Current Year Headlee Millage Reduction Fraction; (7) 2022 Millage Rate Permanently Reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee; (8) Sec. 211.34 Truth in Assessing or Equalization Millage Rollback Fraction; (9) Maximum Allowable Millage Levy; (10) Millage Requested to be Levied July 1; (11) Millage Requested to be Levied Dec. 1; and (12) Expiration Date of Millage Authorized.

Certification. Signature and identification lines are provided for Prepared by, Telephone Number, Title of Preparer and Date. The certification paragraph reads that, as the representatives for the local government unit named above, the signers certify that the requested tax levy rates have been reduced, if necessary, to comply with the state constitution (Article 9, Section 31), and that the requested levy rates have also been reduced, if necessary, to comply with MCL Sections 211.24e, 211.34 and, for LOCAL school districts which levy a Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millage, MCL 380.1211(3). Signature blocks follow for Clerk or Secretary (signature, printed name, date) and Chairperson or President (signature, printed name, date). A starred footnote explains that under Truth in Taxation, MCL Section 211.24e, the governing body may decide to levy a rate which will not exceed the maximum authorized rate allowed in column 9, and that the requirements of MCL 211.24e must be met prior to levying an operating levy larger than the base tax rate but not larger than the rate in column 9.

Local School District Use Only. A separate block, to be completed if requesting millage to be levied and following STC Bulletin 2 of 2022, records Total School District Operating Rates to be Levied (HH/Supp and NH Oper ONLY), with separate rate lines For Principal Residence, Qualified Ag., Qualified Forest and Industrial Personal; For Commercial Personal; and For all Other. A double-starred note directs the filer to the page 2 instructions regarding where to find the millage rate used in column (5).

Instructions for completing Form 614 (L-4029). The instructions are provided under MCL Sections 211.24e (truth in taxation), 211.34 (truth in county equalization and truth in assessing), 211.34d (Headlee), and 211.36 and 211.37 (apportionment).

Column 1, Source: enter the source of each millage, for example allocated millage, separate millage limitations voted, charter, approved extra-voted millage, or public act number; taxes levied on the Industrial Facilities Tax Roll are excluded.

Column 2, Purpose of millage: examples given are operating, debt service, special assessments, school enhancement millage and sinking fund millage. A local school district must separately list operating millages by whether they are levied against ALL PROPERTIES in the school district or against the NON-HOME group of properties, per State Tax Commission Bulletin 2 of 2022. Permitted abbreviations are Operating ALL, short for operating millage levied on ALL PROPERTIES in the local school district such as Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millages and Building and Site Sinking Fund Millages, and Operating NON-HOME, short for operating millage levied on all properties excluding principal residence, qualified agricultural, qualified forest and industrial personal properties, such as the 18 mills in a district which does not levy a Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millage.

Column 3, Date of Election: the month and year of the election for each millage authorized by direct voter approval.

Column 4, Millage Authorized: the allocated rate, charter aggregate rate, extra-voted rate authorized before 1979, each separate rate authorized by voters after 1978, debt service rate and similar, stated before any reductions.

Column 5: the 2021 millage rate permanently reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee rollback. Starting with taxes levied in 1994 the Headlee rollback permanently reduces the maximum rate or rates authorized by law or charter. The 2021 permanently reduced rate is found in column 7 of the 2021 Form L-4029. For operating millage approved by voters after April 30, 2021, the millage approved by voters is entered. For debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction, enter NA.

Column 6, Current Year Millage Reduction Fraction: the fraction certified by the county treasurer for the current year as calculated on Form 2166 (L-4034), 2022 Millage Reduction Fraction Calculations Worksheet, rounded to four decimal places. The fraction shall not exceed 1.0000 for 2022 and future years, preventing any increase or roll up of millage rates. Use 1.0000 for new millage approved by voters after April 30, 2022, and 1.0000 for debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction.

Column 7: the 2022 millage rate permanently reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee rollback, found by multiplying column 5 by column 6 on the 2022 Form L-4029, rounded DOWN to four decimal places, citing STC Bulletin No. 11 of 1999 as supplemented by letter of 6/7/2000. Enter NA for debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction.

Column 8, Section 211.34 Millage Rollback Fraction (Truth in Assessing or Truth in Equalization): listed for each operating rate and rounded to four decimal places. Use 1.0000 for school districts, special assessments and bonded debt retirement levies. Counties, villages and authorities enter the Truth in Equalization Rollback Fraction calculated on STC Form L-4034 as total taxable value based on CEV for all classes divided by total taxable value based on SEV for all classes; use 1.0000 for an authority located in more than one county. Townships and cities enter the Truth in Assessing Rollback Fraction calculated on STC Form L-4034 as total taxable value based on assessed value for all classes divided by total taxable value based on SEV for all classes. The Section 211.34 Millage Rollback Fraction shall not exceed 1.0000.

Column 9, Maximum Allowable Millage Levy: multiply column 7 by column 8 and round DOWN to four decimal places, again citing STC Bulletin No. 11 of 1999 and the letter of 6/7/2000. For debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction, enter the millage from column 4.

Columns 10 and 11, Millage Requested to be Levied: enter the tax rate approved by the unit of local government provided it does not exceed the maximum allowable millage levy in column 9. A millage rate exceeding the base tax rate under Truth in Taxation cannot be requested unless the requirements of MCL 211.24e have been met. A LOCAL school district levying a Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millage shall not levy a Supplemental Millage in excess of that allowed by MCL 380.1211(3). Filers are referred to the memo to assessors dated October 26, 2004 regarding the change in the collection date of certain county taxes.

Column 12, Expiration Date of Millage: enter the month and year on which the millage will expire.

Instructions for completing Form 614 (L-4029). Provided under MCL Sections 211.24e (truth in taxation), 211.34 (truth in county equalization and truth in assessing), 211.34d (Headlee), and 211.36 and 211.37 (apportionment).

Column 1, Source: the source of each millage - allocated millage, separate millage limitations voted, charter, approved extra-voted millage, public act number and similar. Taxes levied on the Industrial Facilities Tax Roll are not included.

Column 2, Purpose of millage: examples include operating, debt service, special assessments, school enhancement millage and sinking fund millage. A local school district must separately list operating millages by whether they are levied against ALL PROPERTIES in the school district or against the NON-HOME group of properties, with reference to State Tax Commission Bulletin 2 of 2022. The abbreviations Operating ALL and Operating NON-HOME may be used. Operating ALL covers operating millage levied on ALL PROPERTIES in the local school district, such as Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millages and Building and Site Sinking Fund Millages. Operating NON-HOME covers operating millage levied on all properties excluding principal residence, qualified agricultural, qualified forest and industrial personal properties, such as the 18 mills in a district which does not levy a Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millage.

Column 3, Date of Election: month and year of the election for each millage authorized by direct voter approval.

Column 4, Millage Authorized: the allocated rate, charter aggregate rate, extra-voted rate authorized before 1979, each separate rate authorized by voters after 1978, debt service rate and similar, before any reductions.

Column 5: the 2021 millage rate permanently reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee rollback. Since taxes levied in 1994 the Headlee rollback permanently reduces the maximum authorized rate or rates. The 2021 permanently reduced rate appears in column 7 of the 2021 Form L-4029. For operating millage approved by voters after April 30, 2021, enter the millage approved by the voters. For debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction, enter NA for not applicable.

Column 6, Current Year Millage Reduction Fraction: the fraction certified by the county treasurer for the current year as calculated on Form 2166 (L-4034), the 2022 Millage Reduction Fraction Calculations Worksheet, rounded to four decimal places. It shall not exceed 1.0000 for 2022 and future years, preventing any increase or roll up of millage rates. Use 1.0000 for new millage approved by voters after April 30, 2022 and for debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction.

Column 7: the 2022 millage rate permanently reduced by MCL 211.34d Headlee rollback, obtained by multiplying column 5 by column 6 on the 2022 Form L-4029 and rounding DOWN to four decimal places, per STC Bulletin No. 11 of 1999 supplemented by letter of 6/7/2000. Enter NA for debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction.

Column 8, Section 211.34 Millage Rollback Fraction (Truth in Assessing or Truth in Equalization): listed for each operating rate and rounded to four decimal places. Use 1.0000 for school districts, special assessments and bonded debt retirement levies. Counties, villages and authorities enter the Truth in Equalization Rollback Fraction calculated on STC Form L-4034 as total taxable value based on CEV for all classes over total taxable value based on SEV for all classes, and use 1.0000 for an authority located in more than one county. Townships and cities enter the Truth in Assessing Rollback Fraction calculated on STC Form L-4034 as total taxable value based on assessed value for all classes over total taxable value based on SEV for all classes. The fraction shall not exceed 1.0000.

Column 9, Maximum Allowable Millage Levy: multiply column 7 by column 8 and round the rate DOWN to four decimal places, per STC Bulletin No. 11 of 1999 supplemented by letter of 6/7/2000. For debt service or special assessments not subject to a millage reduction fraction, enter the millage from column 4.

Columns 10 and 11, Millage Requested to be Levied: enter the tax rate approved by the unit of local government provided it does not exceed the maximum allowable millage levy in column 9. A rate exceeding the base tax rate under Truth in Taxation cannot be requested unless the requirements of MCL 211.24e have been met. A LOCAL school district levying a Supplemental (Hold Harmless) Millage shall not levy a Supplemental Millage in excess of that allowed by MCL 380.1211(3). The instructions refer filers to the memo to assessors dated October 26, 2004 regarding the change in the collection date of certain county taxes.

Column 12, Expiration Date of Millage: the month and year on which the millage will expire.
